messages:
maria: Hey folks — trying to onboard a Next + Edge sample that imports the JS/TS SDK. Node build is fine, but the Edge worker typechecks fail and then runtime blows up with a default import error. Anyone seen SDK overloads cause weird `unknown` vs `any` inference in an ESM/Edge context?

aj: Which SDK entry are you importing? we have separate entrypoints for node vs edge (and historically some overloads lived only on the node entry).

maria: Import line is `import Inference from '@redwood/inference'` (sample template). Types: tsc complains about ambiguous overloads on `generate()` — it picks the `any` overload and then the Edge bundler throws because a node-only retry module sneaks in.

kevin: Two separate problems here: (1) ESM/CJS resolution + package exports mapping, and (2) overload/generic ordering causing inference differences under `nodenext` vs `node` moduleResolution. For (1) check `package.json` in the sample — if `type` is missing or `exports` doesn't map an `./edge` entrypoint bundlers fall back to commonjs files.

sam: Repro tip I used yesterday: in tsconfig for Edge apps use:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "esnext",
    "moduleResolution": "nodenext",
    "target": "ES2022",
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true
  }
}
```

That often aligns tsc with the bundler. But it won't fix SDK overload ordering.

maria: Changing tsconfig to nodenext helped the type errors a bit, but still ambiguous overload on `generate(input)` where inference becomes `any` even though our generic default is `unknown`. Edge types seem pickier.

aj: The root cause: we have two overloads in the typings: one for `generate(prompt: string): Promise<string>` and a generic `generate<T>(input: T): Promise<T>` (simplified). TypeScript chooses the non-generic overload in some resolution modes, which then forces `any` downstream. Reordering or adding a single generic fallback signature that is last can make resolution stable across moduleResolution modes.

kevin: Also worth noting: some of our shipped types used `any` in a couple helper interfaces to keep Node ergonomics. Those leak into consumers when TS falls back to the node entrypoint. We should audit and replace `any` -> `unknown` where reasonable, and provide safe narrowing helpers in the SDK.

maria: Another runtime error: when the bundler pulls in `node:timers` via a retry util, edge worker runtime throws. Is there a published edge entrypoint that tree-shakes away node deps?

sam: Yes — we have an `index.edge.mjs` export but the sample's package.json `exports` didn't point to it. Quick workaround: import from `@redwood/inference/edge` or use `import { edgeClient } from '@redwood/inference/edge'` until we fix exports.

kevin: Actionable items: 1) Update sample template package.json to include `exports` map with `./edge` and `./node` entrypoints. 2) Reorder overloads in `client.d.ts` to put the most generic signature last. 3) Replace internal `any` spots with `unknown` + assertions. 4) Add an Edge CI job that typechecks sample with `moduleResolution: nodenext`.

maria: I'm happy to PR the sample changes. Filed it in the backlog and linked repro: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/122 (draft).

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add edge-types CI job to `samples/.github/workflows/ci.yml` (assigned to @maria).

sam: Minor docs note: add a quick snippet in "Edge onboarding" about `import .../edge` and tsconfig recommendation. That will save the next person 30 minutes. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks all — will send a PR for sample + docs. If someone can volunteer to look at the overload reorder in the SDK typing files that'd be great (kevin?).

kevin: I can take the typing audit after lunch. I'll create a tiny test matrix: TS versions 4.9/5.0/5.1 x moduleResolution node/nodenext to validate.

maria: Sweet — closing the thread once PRs are up.
